messages:
ops-bot: Paging oncall: multiple GPU hosts in cluster-gpu-prod are reporting repeated Xid 13/11 driver resets and a spike in ECC correctable counts. Affected hosts: node-17, node-42, node-58. Automated eviction of pods has begun. Thresholds crossed at 2026-03-15T09:10:00Z.

maya (oncall): seeing the alert now. Adding context: tailing metrics shows a sudden jump in correctable errors on node-17. Latency to pods on that host has spiked ~3-4x.

ashish (eng-sre): confirmed. `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` shows correctable errors incrementing rapidly. Kernel logs show repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13` entries.

jordan (infra): are these hosts recently patched? I see node-17 was kernel-rolling last night but node-42 hasn't touched in two weeks. Could be firmware mismatch.

maya (oncall): customer impact: a handful of live inference jobs reported 5xxs and reconnects. No full degrade of service yet, but autoscaler evicted ~6 pods. Marking as partial impact. @eva can you flag any customer tickets?

eva (support): on it. Opening bridge with affected customers and tagging SLA. put customers A and B on watch.

maya (oncall): quick triage steps: 1) cordon node-17 2) start graceful drain with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node-17` 3) if drain fails due to stuck pods, force evict. Need to avoid making latency worse.

ashish (eng-sre): running `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-17` now to identify heavy GPU long-lived batches. I'm going to throttle batch queueing from the scheduler for that host.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: canary fallback for GPU inference route infra/gpu-infer -> fallback to model-quantized-1 on dedicated-pool-2.

maya (oncall): good. Let's failover traffic away from node-17 regionally if possible. jordan, can you confirm routing?

jordan (infra): routing rules applied: traffic rerouted away from zone-us-west-2a where node-17 sits. Canary rollout confirmed healthy.

ashish (eng-sre): collecting kernel dmesg snippet from node-17: ```Mar 15 09:09:45 node-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=1024, Threaded Context```. Also seeing `EVT: ecc correctable count +134 in 60s`.

maya (oncall): thanks. decision: cordon + drain now. If node continues to generate Xids after drain, we'll reboot and then run firmware probe. If it flaps after reboot, escalate to hardware replacement.

ashish (eng-sre): starting drain. Flagging heavy stateful pods: ml-batch-runner-3 is pinned; planning preemptive checkpoint before eviction.

eva (support): customers updated: low-level impact; some requests saw transient 502s; we advise retry/backoff. Customers requested ETA — will update after host reboot.

maya (oncall): trying a soft reboot sequence if drain completes. @jordan allocate spare host for live pods in that rack.

jordan (infra): provisioning spare GPU host (node-spare-01) and attaching NVMe. ETA ~6m.

deploy-bot: rolling restart of affected DaemonSets started to clear dangling GPU drivers on replacement nodes.

maya (oncall): drain completed for node-17. Evicted 14 pods, 2 failed graceful -> forced. Starting reboot now: `sudo systemctl reboot` issued.

ops-bot: note — autoscaler will not place new pods on cordoned nodes.

ashish (eng-sre): watching driver logs post-reboot. If Xid errors persist on cold boot, next step is to disable GPU power management `echo 0 > /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/no_pm` just for a test window and run stress. Also cross-check GPU BIOS versions.

maya (oncall): reboot succeeded. Node back up but dmesg still shows a low-rate stream of correctable ECCs; not flaring like before.

jordan (infra): BIOS on node-17 is older (v1.2.3) vs fleet baseline v1.3.0. Opening infra ticket to schedule bios update during maintenance window.

ashish (eng-sre): ran `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=retired_pages --format=csv` — no retired pages. Good. Kernel Xid still occasional but below alert threshold.

maya (oncall): marking incident state: mitigated but monitoring. We'll leave node-17 cordoned until next maintenance window to update BIOS/firmware and run extended stress tests.

eva (support): told customers A/B: mitigation in place, routed to fallback, will be cordoned until firmware update. Customers OK for now but requested postmortem.

maya (oncall): @ashish please capture timeline and logs for postmortem. Include `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `smartctl` output for the host NVMe, and PCI device info.

ashish (eng-sre): will do. Suggest adding a new alert rule to correlate rapid ECC correctable increments + Xid 13 bursts to trigger preemptive cordon earlier.

jordan (infra): agree. Also adding a scheduled health-check job to run `nvidia-smi -q` hourly and compare firmware/driver skew across fleet.

maya (oncall): handing off to next oncall @ashish for postmortem and cleanup. I will uncordon only after maintenance complete. Closing paging loop for now. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident status updated to MITIGATED. Incident ID: INC-2026-0315-04. Bridge closed by maya (oncall).
